definition: The same binomial-tree framework used to model underlying asset prices can also be used to model the risk-free interest rate over time.
core_idea: A constant interest rate produces an unremarkable, flat binomial tree on its own, but it becomes essential later as the risk-free leg combined with the underlying's tree to compute a fair option premium.
key_points: Example given: at a 5% interest rate per period, a dollar held at Time t is worth $1.05 at Time t+1
With constant rates the interest rate tree is not interesting by itself, but is later used to derive the correct option premium
relationships: Feeds directly into arbitrage-free replication pricing
